title: LDGM-Based Quantum Codes for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Yumin Li, Kejing Liu, Hanqing Lou, Javier Garcia-Frias
abstract: We construct a new family of Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes using the generator and parity-check matrices of Low-Density Generator Matrix (LDGM) codes, with row operations applied to both matrices in order to achieve the desired quantum rate. Decoding is performed in an iterative manner, by applying message passing over the associated graph, and discrete Density Evolution (DDE) is used to optimize performance in the depolarizing channel. The proposed construction offers high flexibility and easiness in the design, producing quantum codes that possess excellent error correction capabilities. By properly designing the structure of the code, we are able to control and bound the weight of the stabilizer generators to a small value, which results in codes particularly well suited for fault-tolerant quantum computation. At the same time, these codes achieve very good performance in terms of error correction capability.
summary: This paper introduces a method to construct high-performance quantum error-correcting codes by adapting Low-Density Generator Matrix (LDGM) codes into Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) structures. The authors analyze the performance of these codes under depolarizing noise using iterative decoding and Density Evolution, showing that careful structural design can yield excellent fault-tolerance capabilities.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing quantum error-correcting codes suitable for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_result: The authors propose a new family of CSS codes built from LDGM matrices, demonstrating that optimizing the code structure can significantly improve performance thresholds while maintaining low error floors.
method: They construct the codes using row operations on LDGM generator and parity-check matrices, employing iterative message passing decoding (belief propagation) optimized via Discrete Density Evolution (DDE).
model_or_system: The system is a quantum stabilizer code structured as a CSS code. The construction leverages the sparsity of classical LDGM codes to satisfy necessary mathematical constraints for quantum error correction.
key_observables: Residual error rates ($	ext{BER}_1, 	ext{BER}_2$), convergence threshold, and error floor performance under depolarizing noise.
important_parameters: Depolarizing parameter ($p$), LDGM code degree (e.g., $(8, 8)$ to $(12, 12)$), and structural parameters like $N_a$ and $N_b$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the equivalence between iterative message passing decoding simulations and predictions derived from Discrete Density Evolution (DDE).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how optimizing structural parameters ($N_b$) improves thresholds, how code degree affects error floors versus thresholds, and general performance trends across varying noise levels.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the mathematical framework for CSS codes using LDGM matrices (satisfying commutativity conditions) to detailing the decoding process via message passing. It then moves into rigorous performance analysis by simulating residual errors under depolarizing noise, comparing results against DDE predictions while varying structural and code parameters.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of error thresholds and error floors using established coding theory tools (LDGM codes) provides concrete benchmarks for designing robust quantum computation protocols relevant to open quantum systems.
